title: Count K-Reducible Numbers Less Than N
summary: Given a binary string s representing a number n and an integer k, count how many positive integers less than n can be reduced to 1 by applying the operation of replacing the number with the count of its set bits in binary form at most k times.
statement: Given a binary string s representing a number n and an integer k, count how many positive integers less than n can be reduced to 1 by applying the operation of replacing the number with the count of its set bits in binary form at most k times. The result should be modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: s is a 1–800 digit binary representation without leading zeros and 1 <= k <= 5.
A positive x is k-reducible when at most k repeated popcount operations turn it into one.
Count qualifying x strictly below the represented number, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: After the first operation, only the original number’s set-bit count matters.
Precompute reduction depth for each possible count and count smaller binary values with that many ones.
Scan the upper-bound bits; whenever it has one, place zero and choose the remaining ones combinatorially.
The first lower bit partitions all x<s uniquely, and depth(count)+1 gives their exact reduction requirement.
editorial: The first lower bit partitions all x<s uniquely, and depth(count)+1 gives their exact reduction requirement.

tests.explanation: Below seven, only powers of two 1,2,4 reach one in at most one popcount.
Values one through six qualify; seven needs one additional popcount step.
